An Essential Guide to Energy Management Basics

What Is Energy Management — and Why It Matters for Your Home

Energy management is the ongoing process of monitoring, controlling, and optimizing how energy is used — with the goal of cutting waste, reducing costs, and lowering your environmental footprint.

Here’s a quick breakdown:

What Why It Matters
Monitor energy use See exactly where power is being consumed
Control consumption Reduce waste by automating or adjusting loads
Optimize performance Lower costs and improve efficiency over time
Support sustainability Reduce carbon emissions and grid dependence

Energy isn’t cheap. For commercial buildings, energy is the single largest operating expense — representing roughly a third of a typical operating budget. And here’s the alarming part: office buildings waste up to one-third of the energy they consume. That’s not a rounding error — that’s money walking out the door.

For homeowners, the stakes are just as real. Rising utility rates, grid instability, and increasingly complex energy regulations (especially in California) mean that managing your home’s energy is no longer optional — it’s essential.

The good news? Modern energy management tools make it easier than ever to take control.

I’m Joshua Trevithick, Founder and CEO of PROJECT: automate, and over my two decades designing integrated smart home systems across Southern California, energy management has become one of the most requested — and most impactful — components of every home I build. In the sections ahead, I’ll walk you through everything you need to know to get it right.

Understanding the Core Principles of Energy Management

To build an effective energy management strategy, we must first look at how energy is consumed, where it is wasted, and why securing our power supply has become so critical. Whether you are managing a commercial high-rise in Los Angeles CA or a luxury estate in Malibu, the foundational principles remain the same: you cannot manage what you do not measure.

At its core, systematic energy tracking is about shifting from a reactive posture—where you simply pay whatever utility bill arrives at the end of the month—to a proactive posture. By leveraging real-time data, organizations and homeowners can align their daily operations with sustainability targets, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) goals, and cost-reduction mandates.

Defining Energy Use and Waste

In both commercial and residential spaces, a massive portion of monthly operating expenses is driven by pure waste. Globally, building operations currently account for almost 30% of global final energy use and more than a quarter of energy-related CO2 emissions.

For commercial properties, this waste often stems from outdated heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) schedules, faulty building management systems, and lighting left on in unoccupied spaces. In luxury residential properties across Beverly Hills and Bel Air, energy waste frequently occurs due to massive climate zones fighting against solar heat gain, unoptimized pool heating, and entertainment systems drawing constant “vampire” loads. Identifying and eliminating these inefficiencies is the fastest way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while immediately improving your bottom line.

The Importance of Energy Security

Energy security is no longer just a macroeconomic concern; it is a highly localized issue. Grid instability, extreme weather events, and rising peak demands have made the local power grid increasingly vulnerable.

For instance, European corporations historically invest 41% less on information security than American companies, making localized energy security and smart infrastructure solutions exceptionally critical in Europe. However, right here in Southern California, homeowners in areas like Pacific Palisades and Rolling Hills regularly experience grid strain and planned safety power shutoffs. Implementing localized energy security—via solar arrays, battery backup systems, and intelligent load shedding—protects your property from blackouts while shielding you from volatile peak-time utility rates.

The Core Benefits of a Comprehensive Energy Program

Implementing a structured energy management program is one of the few initiatives where environmental responsibility directly translates into financial reward. Let’s look at how optimizing your power consumption impacts both your wallet and your carbon footprint.

Benefit Category Commercial Impact Residential Impact
Financial Yield Decreasing energy use by 10% can lead to a 1.5% increase in net operating income (NOI). Lower monthly utility bills and protection against high Time-of-Use (TOU) rates.
Asset Value Higher building valuation, lower operating budgets, and attractive green building certifications. Increased home resale value and robust energy independence during grid failures.
Sustainability Streamlined ESG reporting and compliance with strict local emissions limits. Drastic reduction in household carbon footprint and seamless integration of clean energy.

Financial and Operational Efficiency

The financial benefits of modern energy tracking go far beyond simple conservation. By using advanced utility tracking software and competitive procurement strategies, businesses can negotiate better energy contracts and avoid expensive peak-demand penalties.

On the operational side, intelligent asset management systems allow for predictive maintenance. By monitoring the electrical draw of critical machinery, HVAC compressors, or pool pumps, the system can detect anomalies before a total equipment failure occurs. If a motor starts drawing 20% more current than normal, the system flags it for maintenance, preventing costly downtime and extending the lifespan of your mechanical investments.

Supporting ESG and Regulatory Compliance

For modern enterprises, tracking carbon output is no longer optional. Regulatory frameworks like the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), EU taxonomy, and local environmental mandates require precise tracking of Scope 1, Scope 2, and even Scope 3 emissions.

Using sophisticated digital platforms allows companies to maintain a single, auditable system of record for energy and emissions data. This transparency is vital for satisfying investors, meeting ESG targets, and demonstrating genuine environmental responsibility. In California, residential projects must also align with strict standards, making compliance a key driver for smart home energy planning.

Key Technologies Driving Modern Energy Systems

The modern energy landscape has moved past manual meter readings and basic programmable thermostats. Today, we rely on a sophisticated ecosystem of hardware and software to orchestrate power distribution seamlessly.

Industrial Energy Management Software and IoT Tools

At the enterprise level, tools like IoT sensors, smart meters, and cloud-based dashboards compile millions of data points into actionable insights. Advanced software platforms allow managers to visualize complex energy flows through Sankey diagrams and heat maps, highlighting exactly where power enters a facility and where it is lost.

To achieve deep optimization, large-scale operators utilize specialized industrial platforms. For example, the ABB Ability Energy Management System provides real-time demand-side optimization, helping industrial plants manage process flexibility and shift heavy loads away from peak pricing periods. Similarly, the SIMATIC Energy Manager from Siemens offers comprehensive, production-level energy monitoring that links energy consumption directly to machine output, allowing operators to meet strict ISO 50001 standards while reducing overall operating costs.

Smart Panels and Residential Energy Management Systems

In high-end residential spaces, the heart of modern energy control is the smart electrical panel. Traditional electrical panels are entirely passive; they contain simple breakers that trip only during an overload. A smart electrical panel, however, utilizes intelligent relay modules to provide circuit-level monitoring and control.

When integrated with home automation, we can program your home to run in an automated “Eco Mode.” During peak utility pricing hours, the system can automatically dim non-essential lighting, adjust the climate control by a couple of degrees, and temporarily pause EV charging.

We can also tie these controls into sophisticated lighting and shading systems. For instance, utilizing Lutron lighting control paired with an exquisite Ketra lighting design allows us to create beautiful, energy-efficient interior environments. By automating motorized shades to lower during the hottest part of the day, we block solar heat gain before it warms your home, drastically reducing the load on your HVAC system without sacrificing design or comfort.

A 7-Step Roadmap for Implementing Energy Best Practices

To achieve sustained, long-term energy savings, you cannot treat energy efficiency as a one-time project. It must be woven directly into your organizational culture or household habits. The most successful programs follow a structured, continuous improvement cycle, heavily inspired by the proven ENERGY STAR Guidelines for Energy Management.

  1. Make Commitment: Secure buy-in from senior leadership (or establish a clear household goal) and appoint an energy director or champion to lead the initiative.
  2. Assess Performance: Collect utility data, conduct thorough energy audits, and benchmark your properties using tools like the Energy Program Assessment Matrix to establish a baseline.
  3. Set Goals: Establish clear, measurable, and realistic targets for energy reduction, cost savings, and carbon emissions.
  4. Create Action Plan: Map out the exact technological upgrades, operational adjustments, and behavioral changes needed to hit your targets.
  5. Implement Action Plan: Install smart monitoring systems, upgrade outdated equipment, and automate your energy-saving scenes.
  6. Evaluate Progress: Regularly compare your post-implementation utility data against your baseline to verify actual savings and refine your strategies.
  7. Recognize Achievements: Celebrate your team’s success, apply for certifications like ISO 50001, and leverage your green credentials to attract eco-conscious clients or tenants.

Overcoming Implementation Challenges Across Different Sectors

While the benefits of modern energy platforms are clear, the path to implementation can present hurdles. Understanding the unique challenges of your specific sector is the first step toward overcoming them.

Industrial and Manufacturing Applications

For industrial facilities, the primary challenge is integrating new energy tracking software with legacy automation systems without disrupting continuous production lines. Industrial processes require extreme reliability; a single unscheduled shutdown can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars.

To solve this, modern systems integrate directly with existing Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) and programmable logic controllers (PLCs). This allows manufacturers to implement proactive load management and peak shaving—temporarily reducing power to non-critical auxiliary machinery during high-demand periods—without impacting the core production schedule.

Commercial Buildings and Smart Homes

For commercial properties and luxury residences in California, navigating complex local building codes and utility structures is a major hurdle. Compliance with California Title 24 energy efficiency requirements is mandatory for new construction and major renovations. Furthermore, the introduction of NEM 3.0 (Net Energy Metering) has fundamentally changed how solar energy is compensated, making solar export to the grid far less lucrative than it used to be.

To maximize your return on investment under these rules, homes must transition from simple solar generation to intelligent storage and load shedding. By automating your home’s thermal boundaries with Crestron Home motorized shades, you can significantly reduce heating and cooling requirements.

Furthermore, we can program a custom energy moment into your home automation system. When the utility rates spike or a planned blackout is initiated, your home instantly adapts: non-essential circuits are shed, motorized shades adjust to block solar heat, and your critical systems transition seamlessly to stored battery power—all without you ever noticing a flicker in your lighting.

Frequently Asked Questions about Energy Management

What is the role of the Energy Management Association?

The Energy Management Association (EMA) is a prominent national organization dedicated to advancing the practice of energy management. They provide professional training, industry-recognized certifications, and education on building performance. Their Energy Management Professional (EMP) certification is highly regarded, helping facility managers and engineers master the latest strategies for optimizing building systems and ensuring long-term energy efficiency.

How do smart home systems protect against California power outages?

Smart home systems, particularly when paired with advanced energy management platforms like Savant Power, protect your home by constantly monitoring the grid’s health. In the event of a planned blackout or grid failure, the system automatically disconnects from the grid and transitions your home to stored battery power within milliseconds.

Because running an entire luxury home on batteries during a multi-day outage is rarely practical, the system automatically initiates a pre-configured backup scene. It prioritizes critical circuits—such as refrigeration, security systems, home offices, and medical equipment—while shedding heavy, non-essential loads like pool heaters and guest-house air conditioning. You also receive instant smartphone alerts keeping you informed of your system’s battery life and power status.

Can energy management systems integrate with existing solar panels?

Absolutely. Modern energy management systems are designed to be highly retrofittable. They can interface with your existing solar arrays and battery storage systems, acting as the intelligent “brain” that coordinates them. Instead of simply letting your solar panels feed power blindly back into the grid, the smart system ensures that solar energy is directed first to power your home’s immediate needs, second to top off your backup battery storage, and third to charge your electric vehicles during the most cost-effective hours.

Conclusion

Taking control of your energy footprint doesn’t mean you have to sacrifice comfort, convenience, or luxury. At PROJECT: automate, we specialize in delivering “invisible intelligence”—bespoke, ultra-discreet home automation solutions that work tirelessly behind the scenes to optimize your property’s performance.

Whether you are looking to secure your estate against unpredictable Southern California blackouts, lower your carbon footprint, or seamlessly navigate complex utility rates, we are here to help. From Venice Beach and Manhattan Beach to Beverly Hills, Malibu, and the Hollywood Hills, we design and install tailored energy solutions that elevate your lifestyle while protecting your home.

Ready to transform how your home utilizes power? Explore our comprehensive energy management services and schedule a complimentary consultation with our team today.

Why the Brilliant Smart Switch is a Bright Idea for Your Home

The Brilliant Smart Switch: A Smarter Way to Control Your Home

Brilliant smart switches are in-wall touchscreen control panels that replace standard light switches and act as a central hub for your entire smart home — controlling lighting, music, cameras, locks, and climate from one device.

Here is a quick overview of what makes them stand out:

Feature Detail
Control panel types 1-switch to 4-switch wired panels, plug-in panel
Smart Dimmer Switch price $69.99 single, as low as $59.99 in bundles
Control panel price range $299 to $749 depending on model
Voice assistants supported Amazon Alexa (built-in), Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit
Key integrations Sonos, Ring, Philips Hue, Ecobee, August Lock, SmartThings
Wiring required Neutral wire and ground wire (120V AC, US only)
Connectivity Wi-Fi + Bluetooth Low Energy mesh network
Works without Wi-Fi? Yes, for local lighting control

If your smart home feels more like a collection of disconnected gadgets than a seamless experience, you are not alone. Most homeowners end up juggling multiple apps, voice assistants on countertops, and switches that only do one thing. The Brilliant system was designed to solve exactly that — putting everything behind a single, intuitive touchscreen mounted right where you already reach for the light switch.

That said, Brilliant is not the only option. Depending on your home and your expectations, it may be a perfect fit — or just a starting point. This guide breaks down everything you need to know.

I’m Joshua Trevithick, Founder and CEO of PROJECT: automate, and with over two decades designing integrated smart homes across Southern California, I’ve evaluated the Brilliant smart switch alongside every major platform on the market. I’ll give you an honest, experience-based look at where Brilliant excels and where a more advanced system might serve you better.

What is the Brilliant Smart Switch and How Does It Work?

At its core, the brilliant smart switch is an in-wall touchscreen control panel designed to replace a standard light switch. Instead of just turning a single light bulb on and off, it serves as a physical, visual bridge for your entire house. Think of it as a localized smart home tablet that lives permanently in your wall, wired directly into your home’s electrical grid.

The system works by combining two distinct types of hardware: the primary Control Panels and the companion Smart Dimmer Switches.

The primary control unit, known as the Brilliant smart home control, features a vibrant 5-inch diagonal LCD touchscreen with a 720×1280 resolution. It connects directly to your home’s 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network to communicate with cloud-based smart home systems, streaming cameras, and smart thermostats.

To expand this control to other rooms without putting an expensive touchscreen in every single wall, Brilliant uses companion Smart Dimmer Switches. These dimmers communicate with the main control panel using an automatic hopping Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Mesh network. This means each dimmer switch acts as a repeater, passing signals along to the next switch. As long as your dimmers are placed within approximately 50 feet (roughly two rooms) of each other or the main panel, they maintain a rock-solid local connection, completely independent of your Wi-Fi signal.

When you walk up to a Brilliant panel, a simple swipe of your finger up or down on the screen adjusts the lights. But because the panel is connected to your local network, that same swipe can be customized to dim your Philips Hue bulbs, adjust your Sonos volume, or trigger a custom “Goodnight” scene that locks your front door and arms your security system.

Key Features and Ecosystem Integrations of Brilliant

The true power of the brilliant smart switch lies in its ability to consolidate multiple smart home systems into one physical interface. If you live in Malibu, Beverly Hills, or Manhattan Beach, you likely have a mix of high-end appliances, security systems, and entertainment setups. Keeping them all organized can be a full-time job.

With a centralized interface, you can manage these disparate technologies from a single wall point. For a broader look at how centralized hardware ties your home together, you can explore our guide on Control Systems.

Let’s explore how the specific components of the Brilliant ecosystem work together.

Centralized Control with the Brilliant Smart Switch Panel

The main Control Panel is the brain of the operation. Available in configurations that fit into 1-gang, 2-gang, 3-gang, or 4-gang electrical boxes, it directly replaces your existing light switches.

Key features built into every main panel include:

  • Built-in Amazon Alexa: The panel features an integrated microphone and speaker, allowing you to use voice commands without cluttering your kitchen countertops with smart speakers.
  • Video Intercom and Camera: A built-in camera allows for room-to-room video intercom calls between multiple Brilliant panels. If you want to call the kids down for dinner in your Hollywood Hills home, you can do it right from the kitchen wall.
  • Physical Privacy Shutter: For peace of mind, a physical slide switch allows you to completely cover the camera lens and disable the microphone.
  • Motion Detection: The panel uses built-in motion sensors to automatically turn the screen on when you walk into a room, and turn it off (or dim it to act as a digital photo frame) when the room is empty.

Expanding Your Network with the Brilliant Smart Switch Dimmer

The Brilliant Smart Dimmer Switch is the workhorse of the system. Priced at $69.99 (and as low as $59.99 in multi-packs), it allows you to bring smart lighting control to every room in your house without buying a touchscreen for every wall.

These dimmers support up to 500W of incandescent/halogen lighting or up to 200W of LED/CFL lighting. They feature capacitive touch sliders, allowing you to dim the lights by sliding your finger up or down the physical switch.

Additionally, the dimmer includes:

  • Double-Tap Scene Activation: You can program a double-tap on the physical switch to trigger custom scenes. For example, double-tapping the bedroom switch can turn off all house lights, set the thermostat, and lock the doors.
  • Built-in Motion Sensors: Like the main panel, each dimmer has a motion sensor that can be configured to turn lights on when you enter and off after a set period of inactivity.
  • Smart Bulb Compatibility: If you use smart bulbs like Philips Hue or LIFX, you can configure the Brilliant switch to maintain constant power to the bulb while sending wireless dimming commands. This prevents the common issue of smart bulbs becoming unresponsive when someone flips the physical wall switch.

To understand how advanced dimmer configurations can elevate your interior design and lighting layers, read our comprehensive overview of Light Control.

Installation Requirements and Setup Process

Installing a brilliant smart switch is designed to be a straightforward DIY project for those comfortable with basic electrical work, though professional installation is always recommended for multi-gang boxes or complex configurations.

Before you purchase, you must verify your home’s wiring. The wired Brilliant Control Panels and Smart Dimmer Switches require a standard 120V AC electrical system and must have both a neutral wire and a ground wire present in the electrical box.

Most homes built in the mid-1980s or later in areas like Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades, or Studio City will have neutral wires throughout. However, if you live in an older, historic home in Los Angeles, you may need to consult an electrician to pull neutral wires to your switch boxes.

The physical installation process generally follows these steps:

  1. Turn off the power: Always shut off the circuit breaker controlling the switch before starting.
  2. Remove the old switch: Unscrew the existing switch and take a picture of the wiring configuration for reference.
  3. Connect the wires: Wire the Brilliant baseplate using the provided wire connectors. The switch is intelligent enough to automatically identify line and load wires, but you must manually connect the neutral and ground wires.
  4. Mount the baseplate: Screw the base plate into the electrical box.
  5. Attach the faceplate: Snap the touchscreen faceplate onto the baseplate.
  6. Configure on-screen: Turn the power back on. The touchscreen will boot up and guide you through connecting to your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network, testing your lights for flicker, and linking your third-party smart home accounts.

For official, step-by-step documentation and videos on this process, you can refer to the Brilliant – Installation Smart Home Control page.

Pricing, Bundles, and Target Audience

The Brilliant ecosystem is highly modular, allowing you to start small and expand over time. Most users begin with a starter bundle and gradually add dimmers as their needs grow.

Here is a breakdown of the typical pricing and bundle options available:

  • 1-Switch Control Panel (NextGen): $599.00
  • 2-Switch Control Panel (NextGen): $649.00
  • 3-Switch Control Panel (NextGen): $699.00
  • 4-Switch Control Panel (NextGen): $749.00
  • Plug-In Control Panel Bundle (Includes 2 Smart Plugs): $299.00
  • Smart Dimmer Switch: $69.99 (Single unit)
  • Brilliant Smart Plug: $29.00

Because the Smart Dimmer Switches rely on a main Control Panel to function, Brilliant offers “Starter Packs” that bundle a control panel with three dimmer switches. This is often the most cost-effective way to outfit a main living area or primary suite.

Who is Brilliant Best Suited For?

  • Tech-Savvy Homeowners: If you love smart home technology but want a clean, unified way for family members and guests to control the house without needing a smartphone app, Brilliant is an exceptional solution.
  • Modern Builders: For builders constructing new homes in Rancho Palos Verdes or Rolling Hills, installing Brilliant panels during construction adds a premium, high-tech feature that instantly appeals to modern buyers.
  • Renters (Plug-In Option): The Plug-In Control Panel mounts flush to any wall and plugs into a standard outlet via a 13-foot USB cord. It requires no electrical wiring or neutral wires, making it perfect for luxury apartments in Hermosa Beach or Redondo Beach where modifying the electrical system is not allowed.

Comparing Brilliant to Traditional and Luxury Smart Switches

While the brilliant smart switch is an impressive consumer-grade solution, it occupies a middle ground between basic DIY smart switches (like Lutron Caséta or standard Z-Wave switches) and professional, luxury lighting control systems like Lutron HomeWorks or Savant.

If you are designing a high-end estate in Bel Air or Beverly Hills, you may want to consider how Brilliant compares to a bespoke architectural solution. Luxury systems focus on “invisible intelligence”—hiding bulky equipment in remote closets and using elegant, minimalist keypads on the wall rather than glowing touchscreens in every room.

To understand the differences between these approaches, it is helpful to look at the wiring and design philosophies behind them. You can read more about these design choices in our article, Should I Choose Lutron Wired or Wireless Lighting Control?.

For luxury projects, interior designers often prefer customized keypads that blend seamlessly into plaster, stone, or wood walls. To see why this collaboration is so critical, check out Why Interior Designers Should Partner with a Lutron Dealer.

Here is a direct comparison of how Brilliant stacks up against basic smart switches and luxury architectural systems:

Feature Standard Smart Switches (e.g., Lutron Caséta) Brilliant Smart Switch System Luxury Lighting Systems (e.g., Lutron HomeWorks)
Primary Interface Physical plastic buttons 5-inch LCD Touchscreen & Dimmers Bespoke architectural metal/glass keypads
Central Hub Needed? Yes (external bridge) No (panel acts as the hub) Yes (centralized processor)
Wall Clutter High (requires multiple switches side-by-side) Medium (consolidates 1-4 switches into one panel) Extremely Low (centralized panels hide switches in closets)
Integrations Limited to lighting and basic scenes Excellent (Sonos, Ring, Nest, Hue, locks, etc.) Unlimited (AV, climate, pool, shades, security, gates)
Aesthetic Customization Standard white/almond plastic plates Interchangeable colored frames Custom finishes (brass, bronze, glass, flush-mount)
Reliability High (Clear Connect wireless) Medium-High (Wi-Fi and BLE Mesh) Professional Grade (Hardwired or dedicated RF)

If you are exploring luxury options that offer deep integration with high-end audio-visual and automation systems, you might also want to look into how we Offer Clients Intuitive Control with Savant Systems.

Frequently Asked Questions about Smart Lighting Control

Does the Brilliant Smart Dimmer Switch require a control panel?

Yes. The Brilliant Smart Dimmer Switch does not have its own Wi-Fi radio. Instead, it relies on a local Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Mesh network to communicate. To function as a smart device, at least one wired or plug-in Brilliant Control Panel must be installed in your home. The dimmer switches must be placed within approximately 50 feet (or two rooms) of the control panel or another dimmer node to maintain a reliable connection.

Will my Brilliant switches work if the Wi-Fi goes down?

Yes, but with limitations. Because the switches communicate with each other locally via a Bluetooth mesh network, your physical light switches, dimming functions, and motion sensors will continue to work perfectly even if your internet service provider goes down. However, any features that require an internet connection—such as viewing your Ring doorbell feed, adjusting your Nest thermostat, playing Sonos music, using Alexa voice control, or controlling your lights remotely via the mobile app—will be unavailable until your Wi-Fi is restored.

Can I install Brilliant switches in an older home without a neutral wire?

If you want to use the standard, in-wall wired Control Panels or Smart Dimmer Switches, neutral and ground wires are strictly required. If your home was built before the mid-1980s and has not been rewired, you likely do not have neutral wires behind your switches.

However, you still have options:

  1. The Plug-In Control Panel: You can purchase the Brilliant Plug-In Panel, which mounts to any wall without an electrical box and plugs into a standard outlet. This allows you to use the touchscreen interface to control wireless smart bulbs (like Philips Hue) and smart plugs throughout your home without needing neutral wires in your walls.
  2. Professional Rewiring: You can work with a professional team to run neutral wires to key switch locations in your home, allowing you to install the fully integrated wired system.

Conclusion

The brilliant smart switch is an exceptional, highly innovative solution for homeowners who want to clean up their walls, eliminate countertop clutter, and establish an intuitive, family-friendly control point for their smart devices. By replacing standard switches with elegant touchscreens, Brilliant makes daily interactions with your home feel seamless and modern.

However, for luxury estates in neighborhoods like Malibu, Beverly Hills, or Palos Verdes, a touchscreen on every wall isn’t always the right aesthetic choice. True luxury automation is about “invisible intelligence”—technology that works flawlessly in the background, leaving your home’s architecture and interior design to take center stage.

Whether you are looking to install a modular system like Brilliant or design a fully integrated, bespoke architectural lighting system, we are here to help. At PROJECT: automate, we specialize in custom Light Control and automation solutions tailored perfectly to your lifestyle.

Ready to transform your home with intelligent lighting? Connect with our team here to start a conversation about your project.

Is Your Building Burning Cash? How BMS Upgrades Actually Save Energy

Why Building Management System Energy Savings Matter More Than Ever

Building management system energy savings are real, measurable, and significant — and the numbers back that up.

Here’s a quick summary of what the research shows:

Scenario Energy Savings
Properly tuned controls across all commercial buildings Up to 29% reduction
Adjusting temperature setpoints alone ~8% reduction
Occupancy-based HVAC scheduling ~6% reduction
Reducing minimum VAV airflow rates ~7% reduction
Secondary schools with full controls Up to 49% reduction
Standalone retail with full controls Up to 41% reduction
State-of-the-art BEMS (conservative estimate) 5–10% of utility bill

And it’s not just percentages. Buildings are responsible for 28% of global CO2 emissions. Up to 60% of U.S. commercial floor space still lacked any building automation system as recently as 2012. That’s an enormous amount of energy — and money — being wasted every day.

The problem isn’t that the technology doesn’t exist. It does. The problem is that most buildings are still running on static schedules, manual overrides, and aging control systems that have no idea whether anyone is actually inside.

That gap between what buildings consume and what they need to consume — that’s where the opportunity lives.

I’m Joshua Trevithick, Founder and CEO of PROJECT: automate, and over two decades of designing intelligent building and home systems — including integrated climate control and energy management solutions — I’ve seen how the right controls transform both comfort and building management system energy savings. In the sections ahead, I’ll walk you through exactly how these systems work, what real-world results look like, and how to evaluate whether an upgrade makes financial sense for your property.

BMS vs. BAS: Evolution of Intelligent Building Controls

To understand how modern properties unlock deep efficiency, we must first clear up some industry alphabet soup. For years, properties relied on a Building Automation System (BAS) to handle basic mechanical tasks. A traditional BAS is primarily concerned with execution: turning on a chiller at 6:00 AM, keeping a boiler running until 6:00 PM, and ensuring basic airflow.

However, as we look at the landscape in July 2026, the industry has evolved. Today, we focus on the Building Energy Management System (BEMS), which works in tandem with modern Building Management Systems (BMS). While a BAS acts as the “muscle” (executing physical commands), a BEMS is the “brain.” It layers advanced software, data visualization, and predictive optimization over your existing physical infrastructure.

Under frameworks like the European Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD) and Technical Building Systems (TBS) guidelines, a true BEMS does not just run a schedule; it continuously analyzes energy performance. It integrates utility meters, weather feeds, and indoor air quality sensors to make real-time operational decisions.

This evolution is heavily driven by academic and engineering breakthroughs. For instance, a landmark study published in Scientific Reports highlights how integrating Building Information Modeling (BIM) with the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) allows systems to predict thermal behavior with incredible accuracy. By mapping physical spaces digitally, modern systems can run complex thermodynamic simulations to optimize HVAC loads before a single watt of electricity is wasted.

For our clients in Southern California—spanning luxury estates in Malibu, high-end commercial spaces in Beverly Hills, and modern offices in Manhattan Beach—this shift from reactive automation to predictive energy management is the key to stopping utility bill inflation. You can learn more about how these hardware and software layers interact in our guide to Control Systems.

Maximizing Building Management System Energy Savings: Core Strategies

How do these systems actually keep cash from flying out of your windows? It comes down to a few core control measures that target the heaviest energy consumers in any building: heating, cooling, and ventilation.

According to a comprehensive Department of Energy report, implementing currently developed and properly tuned controls can cut commercial building energy consumption by an average of 29%. Nationally, that is equivalent to saving 4 to 5 Quads of energy—roughly 5% of the entire country’s energy consumption.

When we break down that 29% potential, several high-impact strategies stand out:

  • Setpoint Optimization (~8% Savings): Traditional systems keep indoor temperatures completely static. Setpoint optimization dynamically adjusts temperatures based on external weather and actual indoor needs—such as raising cooling setpoints slightly on hot afternoons or lowering heating targets during unoccupied night hours.
  • Airflow Reduction (~7% Savings): Many commercial systems blast air through Variable Air Volume (VAV) boxes at maximum rates regardless of demand. Reducing minimum airflow rates to match actual ventilation requirements prevents over-conditioning and slashes fan energy.
  • Occupancy-Based Scheduling (~6% Savings): Instead of running HVAC systems on rigid calendar schedules, occupancy-based controls limit heating and cooling to times when spaces are actually in use.

By combining these strategies, certain property types see even more dramatic results. The DOE report notes that secondary schools can achieve up to 49% energy savings, while standalone retail stores and auto dealerships can reach up to 41% savings. Whether managing a commercial boutique in Santa Monica or a sprawling private compound in Bel Air, these numbers show that precision control is always more profitable than brute-force conditioning.

How AI and IoT Drive Building Management System Energy Savings

The modern gold standard for building efficiency relies on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT). By deploying dense networks of wireless IoT sensors, a BEMS can gather granular data—such as localized temperature, relative humidity, and real-time occupancy—every 90 seconds.

This data feeds into advanced AI engines that utilize Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODE) and reinforcement learning to build a “digital twin” of the building’s thermal dynamics. Instead of waiting for a space to overheat, the system predicts solar heat gain hours in advance and pre-cools the building using cheaper, off-peak energy.

This level of predictive control ensures that comfort is never compromised. In fact, by smoothing out temperature swings, AI-driven systems frequently reduce tenant comfort complaints while simultaneously driving down energy consumption. To explore how we design these intelligent, self-optimizing systems, read our comprehensive overview of modern Energy Management.

Standards and Efficiency Classes: The Role of EN 15232

To provide a structured way to measure these technologies, international standards like EN 15232 define four distinct efficiency classes for building automation and control systems:

  • Class A (High Performance): Networked building automation with coordinated, demand-controlled room systems and continuous energy monitoring.
  • Class B (Advanced): Coordinated control systems with some energy monitoring capabilities.
  • Class C (Standard Reference): Basic, non-networked building automation systems.
  • Class D (Non-Efficient): Legacy systems without automatic controls or energy-saving functions.

Upgrading a property from Class D or C to Class A can yield massive, predictable drops in both thermal and electrical energy use. As detailed in the REHVA presentation on BMS impact, utilizing standardized control libraries and synchronized, web-enabled controllers ensures that these savings are durable and do not degrade over time due to programming errors or manual overrides.

Real-World Proof: Case Studies in Building Management System Energy Savings

The theory behind smart controls is compelling, but the real-world data is where the true business case is built.

Consider the documented performance of a 32-story, 480,000-square-foot Class A office tower featured in an Oxmaint case study. Spending $1.4 million annually on HVAC costs, the property deployed an IoT sensor network alongside AI-driven setpoint optimization.

The results after 16 months were staggering:

  • 28% reduction in HVAC energy costs, saving $392,000 annually.
  • 74% reduction in tenant thermal comfort complaints, with zone temperature variances tightening from ±4.2°F to ±1.1°F.
  • 29% improvement in chiller plant efficiency, dropping energy intensity from 0.72 kW/ton to 0.51 kW/ton.
  • 71% reduction in off-hours energy waste by implementing occupancy-triggered setbacks.

Similarly, real-time energy management (RTEM) upgrades across commercial portfolios have shown incredible returns. When a major real estate firm upgraded its portfolio from an older platform to NantumOS, they achieved weather-normalized savings of up to 16.8% during occupied weekdays and over 22% during weekends and holidays. The system achieved this by integrating security turnstile data to track occupancy, allowing the mechanical plant to automatically ramp down during lunch hours and early evenings.

These case studies prove that you do not need to replace your entire mechanical infrastructure to see massive improvements. By layering intelligent software over existing systems, you can unlock what we call an Energy Moment—the exact point where technology, efficiency, and operational savings align.

Multifamily and Commercial Success Stories

These strategies are equally effective in residential and multifamily environments. As reported by Canary Media, real estate giant AvalonBay invested $280,000 in HVAC optimization software across three multifamily buildings. The software bypassed rigid calendar schedules, instead using real-time weather forecasts to modulate central boilers and pumps.

This investment yielded:

  • Over $540,000 in utility savings, more than double their initial target.
  • A rapid 16-month payback period.
  • A reduction of over 1,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions.
  • An additional $30,000 earned by participating in utility demand-response programs.

On a global scale, even super-efficient properties can find room for improvement. In Singapore, the Green Mark Platinum Keppel Bay Tower achieved an additional 7% annual energy savings solely through operational tuning and BMS optimization. As detailed in the IES Keppel Bay Tower case study, engineers built a calibrated “Digital Twin” to test low-cost measures like thermostat adjustments, variable air volume settings, and chiller sequencing before implementing them in the physical building.

Financial Blueprint: Costs, Payback Periods, and ROI

Deploying a BEMS is a capital investment, and like any investment, it must be justified by its return. Fortunately, the financial blueprint for these systems is incredibly robust.

For a typical commercial property, the average cost to deploy a basic BEMS ranges from €20 to €30 per square meter (or equivalent local currency rates). For a standard 10,000 m² (approximately 107,000 sq ft) building, this translates to an initial investment of roughly €250,000.

However, because heating, ventilation, lighting, and electrical loads are managed so much more efficiently, that same building can realistically expect annual utility savings of €50,000 to €80,000. This brings the simple payback period down to a highly attractive 3 to 5 years.

Building Type & Size Estimated Investment Annual Savings Payback Period
Mid-Size Office (10,000 m²) €250,000 €50,000 – €80,000 3.1 – 5 Years
Large Office Tower (480,000 sq ft) $940,000 $392,000 2.4 Years
Multifamily Complex (3 Buildings) $280,000 $540,000 (cumulative) 1.3 Years
Standalone Retail / Supermarket €40,000 €30,700 1.3 Years

To accelerate this return on investment, property owners should leverage utility incentives. Across the country, programs offer substantial rebates for upgrading control sequences and enrolling in demand-response networks. For example, the Mass Save BMS incentives guide outlines prescriptive rebates of up to $0.10 per square foot for new BMS installations and $0.05 per square foot for upgrading existing systems, alongside bonuses for active demand-response enrollment.

Here in Southern California, similar incentives are offered by local utilities like Southern California Edison (SCE) and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP). These programs significantly offset upfront capital expenditures, making BEMS upgrades one of the most financially sound operational improvements a property owner can make.

Overcoming Barriers to BMS Adoption and Long-Term Success

Despite the clear financial and environmental benefits, many properties still hesitate to upgrade. Understanding these barriers is the first step toward overcoming them.

One of the most persistent hurdles is the landlord-tenant split incentive. In many commercial leases, the landlord is responsible for capital improvements (like upgrading a BMS), but the tenants pay the utility bills directly. This leaves the landlord with little motivation to invest in efficiency.

To solve this, progressive property managers are utilizing “green leases,” which allow landlords to recover capital costs from tenants in exchange for guaranteed, lower utility expenses.

Another common issue is operational drift. Over time, building engineers might manually override automated schedules to resolve a temporary tenant complaint, only to leave those overrides active permanently. Within a few years, a highly efficient system can drift back into a high-waste state.

To prevent this, we recommend following the best practices outlined in the Cimetrics guide on optimizing BMS. Successful long-term operations require:

  • Continuous Sensor Calibration: A temperature sensor that is off by just one degree can cause a chiller plant to run hours longer than necessary.
  • Operator Training: Ensuring your facilities team understands why schedules are set up prevents unnecessary manual overrides.
  • Frictionless Visualization: Utilizing clean, simple dashboards makes it easy for management to spot anomalies and energy spikes before they impact the bottom line.

Frequently Asked Questions about BMS Energy Savings

Does AI-driven HVAC optimization require replacing the existing BAS?

No. Modern AI-driven optimization platforms do not require a costly, ground-up replacement of your existing Building Automation System. Instead, they act as a software overlay. Using secure API integrations and open communication protocols like BACnet, the AI engine reads data from your legacy system, calculates optimal setpoints, and writes those commands back to the existing hardware without interrupting daily operations.

What is the typical payback period for a commercial BEMS deployment?

While payback periods vary based on building size, baseline efficiency, and local utility rates, most optimized BEMS deployments achieve full ROI within 18 months to 3.5 years. When factoring in utility rebates, demand-response incentives, and reduced maintenance costs (due to less wear and tear on mechanical equipment), the payback timeline often shrinks even further.

How does a BEMS support regulatory compliance like Local Law 97?

While NYC’s Local Law 97 is a famous example of strict municipal carbon limits, California properties face their own rigorous standards, including Title 24 building energy efficiency mandates and local municipal carbon-reduction goals (such as those in Hermosa Beach). A BEMS directly supports compliance by cutting energy use—and therefore greenhouse gas emissions—by up to 30%. It also generates automated, audit-ready ESG reports aligned with standards like ISO 50001, protecting property owners from costly non-compliance penalties.

Conclusion

Whether you are managing a commercial office building in downtown Los Angeles, a boutique retail space in Venice Beach, or a multi-million dollar private estate in Beverly Hills, the question is no longer whether you can afford to upgrade your control systems—it is whether you can afford to keep letting your current system burn cash.

How to Turn Your House Into a Genius with Brilliant Home Control

What Is Brilliant Home Control — and Is It Right for Your Home?

Brilliant home control is an in-wall smart home system that replaces standard light switches with touchscreen panels, giving you unified control over lighting, music, security, climate, and more — all from one intuitive interface.

Here’s a quick overview of what Brilliant offers:

Feature Details
Control method In-wall touchscreen, voice (Alexa built-in), mobile app
Main products 1–4 switch wired panels, plug-in panel, smart dimmer switches
Key integrations Sonos, Ring, Philips Hue, Ecobee, Google Nest, August Lock
Voice assistants Amazon Alexa (built-in), Google Assistant, Apple HomeKit/Siri
Pricing $599–$749 for wired panels; $9.99/month for Brilliant Max automation
Installation DIY-friendly; requires neutral wire for wired panels
Best for Homeowners, home builders, light-to-mid-level smart home setups

If you’ve ever walked into a home where the lights, music, locks, and thermostat all feel like separate islands — each with its own app, remote, or voice command — you already understand the problem Brilliant set out to solve.

The idea is simple: one panel on the wall that ties everything together. No countertop speakers cluttering your kitchen. No fumbling through five apps to set the mood for dinner. Just a sleek touchscreen where your whole home is a tap or a voice command away.

That promise is what’s made Brilliant one of the more talked-about names in consumer smart home technology since the company launched in 2016. But the road hasn’t been smooth. A near-collapse in 2024, a private acquisition, and a full hardware refresh mean the Brilliant of 2026 looks quite different from the one that first shipped panels nearly a decade ago.

I’m Joshua Trevithick, Founder and CEO of PROJECT: automate, with over two decades of experience designing fully integrated smart home systems for discerning homeowners across Southern California. I’ve evaluated Brilliant home control alongside enterprise-grade platforms like Crestron, Lutron, and Savant — and I’ll give you an honest breakdown of where it fits and where it falls short.

Understanding the Power of Brilliant Home Control

At its core, the Brilliant Smart Home System is designed to make home automation accessible to everyone — not just tech-savvy enthusiasts, but kids, grandparents, and houseguests alike. By replacing a standard multi-gang light switch with an elegant, wall-mounted touchscreen, it establishes a physical command center right where you naturally look for a light switch.

This in-wall panel serves as a centralized hub. Instead of walking into a dark living room and shouting commands at a countertop smart speaker, you can simply swipe up on the screen to bring up the lights. The system coordinates your disparate smart devices over your home’s local Wi-Fi network, allowing you to manage multiple brands of smart lights, music systems, locks, and thermostats from a single, unified interface. To explore their full range of technical capabilities, you can visit the official website for Smart Home Control & Home Automation Technologies | Brilliant.

Every Brilliant Control is packed with utility. It features a high-resolution touchscreen, built-in Amazon Alexa for voice control, a motion sensor for automated lighting, and a camera with a physical privacy shutter. By combining these sensors into a single wall plate, Brilliant eliminates “wall clutter”—the unfortunate aesthetic where a thermostat, intercom, light switch, and voice assistant all fight for real estate on the same wall.

The Core Features of Brilliant Home Control

What makes the brilliant home control system uniquely functional for day-to-day living? It comes down to several core features engineered directly into the hardware:

  • Camera Shutter & Privacy: Every panel includes a built-in camera, but Brilliant understands that privacy is paramount. A physical slider lets you completely block the camera lens when it is not in use.
  • Two-Way Talk & Intercom: When you have multiple Brilliant panels installed throughout your home, they function as a seamless, room-to-room video intercom system. You can easily broadcast announcements to the entire house or have a private two-way video chat with someone in the kitchen while you are in the upstairs bedroom.
  • Digital Photo Frame: When the screen is idle, it doesn’t have to be a blank black rectangle. You can upload up to 25 personal photos via the mobile app, transforming the wall control into a beautiful digital photo frame that showcases your favorite memories.
  • Scene Control: Brilliant allows you to group multiple smart home actions into a single tap. For instance, a “Good Night” scene can simultaneously turn off all downstairs lights, lock the front door, lower the thermostat, and turn off the music.

The Evolution of Brilliant Home Control: From 2024 Acquisition to 2026

To understand where Brilliant stands today in July 2026, we have to look back at its recent corporate history. Founded in 2016 by a team of silicon valley entrepreneurs, the company enjoyed years of steady growth but struggled with the high overhead costs of consumer retail distribution and hardware development.

In May of 2024, the smart home community was shocked when Brilliant announced it had run out of money and was poised to go belly up. For several months, the future of the platform — and the cloud servers required to keep existing installations running — hung in the balance.

Fortunately, the story didn’t end there. In August of 2024, a group of private investors who believed in the product’s potential purchased Brilliant. This acquisition sparked a massive financial recovery and a strategic pivot.

Instead of burning capital to fight for shelf space at mass-market retailers, Brilliant stopped selling its panels on Amazon, Best Buy, and Home Depot. Today, the company sells directly to end-users through its website and focuses heavily on professional channels, partnering with home builders, electrical contractors, and custom integrators to pre-install the systems in new construction and major renovations. This shift has stabilized the brand, allowing them to release their highly anticipated second-generation hardware.

Hardware, Installation, and Integrations of the Brilliant System

One of Brilliant’s greatest selling points is that it fits into standard electrical boxes without requiring custom, low-voltage wiring. However, because it deals with live high-voltage electrical lines, understanding the physical installation requirements is essential before making a purchase.

To help you understand how the hardware has evolved, here is a comparison of the classic generation versus the newly released second-generation hardware:

Hardware Spec Gen 1 (Classic) Gen 2 (NextGen)
Processor Standard Quad-Core High-Performance Upgraded Processor
Wi-Fi Connectivity 2.4 GHz only Dual-Band (2.4 GHz & 5 GHz)
Screen Resolution 720×1280 (Standard) 720×1280 (4x Sharper Image Quality)
Power Options 120V AC Wired 120V AC Wired & Power over Ethernet (PoE)
Performance Moderate lag under heavy load Fluid, highly responsive transitions

For a complete look at their updated hardware specs, you can check out the official Smart Home Control & Home Automation Technologies | Brilliant product pages.

Wired Brilliant controls require a standard 120V AC 60Hz electrical connection. Crucially, your home’s electrical boxes must be up to code, containing a neutral wire and a ground wire in addition to the standard line and load wires. Homes built from the mid-1980s onward generally have neutral wires, but older properties may require an electrician to pull new wires before installation.

Additionally, Brilliant fully supports multi-way (3-way or 4-way) switching. This means you can install a Brilliant panel at one end of a hallway and use standard, non-dimming switches or Brilliant Smart Dimmer Switches at the other end to control the same set of lights.

Main Products and NextGen Upgrades

The Brilliant ecosystem is built around a modular lineup of panels and accessories designed to fit different wall configurations:

  • Wired Control Panels (1 to 4-Switch models): These units replace standard light switch boxes. A 1-Switch panel fits a single-gang box, while a 4-switch panel fits a four-gang box, replacing four individual physical switches with a single touchscreen and physical dimming sliders.
  • Smart Dimmer Switches: These are smaller, traditional-looking switches that connect wirelessly to your main Brilliant panel. They feature built-in motion sensors and support double-tap scene activation, making them perfect for secondary rooms like hallways, bathrooms, or guest bedrooms.
  • Smart Plugs: These plug into standard wall outlets, allowing you to bring traditional floor lamps, fans, or holiday decorations into your Brilliant scenes.

The second-generation hardware features a massive processor bump, which completely eliminates the sluggishness and occasional latency that plagued the original models. The screen is sharper, the touch response is instantaneous, and the inclusion of dual-band Wi-Fi ensures a much more stable connection to your home network. Furthermore, Brilliant has introduced Power over Ethernet (PoE) models, which allow professional installers to power the panels over low-voltage category cabling — a massive win for new construction projects.

Plug-In Control Panel Option

What if you live in an older home without neutral wires, or you are renting an apartment in Venice Beach or West Hollywood and can’t modify the electrical wiring? Brilliant has an elegant solution: the Plug-In Control Panel.

This model requires no complex wiring or electrical boxes. It mounts flush to any wall using a simple mounting plate and draws power from a standard 110V wall outlet via an ultra-thin, 13-foot USB power cord that can be run along the wall or tucked behind the drywall. The plug-in model is often sold as a bundle with two smart plugs, allowing you to instantly establish a smart home command center in any room with zero electrical expertise required.

Supported Smart Home Platforms and Devices

A control system is only as good as the devices it can talk to. Brilliant excels here by offering native, cloud-to-cloud or local network integrations with many of the most popular smart home brands:

  • Smart Speakers & Audio: Deep integration with Sonos and BluOS allows you to browse playlists, adjust volume, and group speakers directly from the wall panel.
  • Video Doorbells & Security: When someone rings your Ring Video Doorbell, the live video feed automatically pops up on the Brilliant screen, allowing you to see who is there and talk to them without picking up your phone. It also integrates with Resideo Total Connect security systems and smart locks from Yale, Schlage, and August.
  • Smart Lighting: Native control for Philips Hue, LIFX, and TP-Link Kasa smart bulbs.
  • Climate Integration: Full compatibility with Google Nest, Ecobee, and Honeywell Home smart thermostats.

Comparing Brilliant to Competitors: Pros, Cons, and Pricing

When planning a smart home, it is important to match the control system to the scale and architectural demands of the property. While Brilliant is an excellent option for retrofits and moderate smart homes, it occupies a very different market space than enterprise-grade automation platforms.

To understand where different systems shine, it helps to look at the broader landscape of Control Systems. For instance, developers and homeowners often weigh whether to invest in bespoke, hardwired platforms or modular, wireless solutions. You can read more about why professional grade systems are favored in luxury developments in our guide on Why Builders Are Including Crestron Installations in Their Homes. Similarly, when focusing specifically on lighting, homeowners must choose between different control topologies, as detailed in our analysis: Should I Choose Lutron Wired or Wireless Lighting Control?.

Here is a quick look at how these systems compare across key metrics:

  • DIY vs. Professional Infrastructure: Brilliant is a wireless, IP-based system that communicates over consumer-grade Wi-Fi. Systems like Crestron and Savant rely on dedicated, hardwired control processors and proprietary communication protocols for absolute reliability.
  • Customization: Brilliant offers a clean, fixed user interface that is easy to navigate but cannot be customized. Luxury systems offer fully bespoke user interfaces tailored to the exact architectural layout of your estate.
  • Scale: Brilliant is ideal for standard single-family homes or apartments. For massive multi-structure estates in Malibu or Bel Air with complex HVAC, pool controls, home theaters, and motorized shades, a professional automation platform is required.

Brilliant vs. Crestron and Savant

For high-end residential projects in Southern California, we frequently specify Savant and Crestron. These platforms represent the pinnacle of bespoke home automation. If you want to learn more about how Savant unifies these complex systems, read our article on how to Offer Clients Intuitive Control with Savant Systems.

While Brilliant replaces a light switch with a small consumer touchscreen, Crestron and Savant handle whole-home distribution of uncompressed 4K video, audiophile-grade architectural sound, complex climate zoning, and automated shading systems that adjust in real-time based on the sun’s position.

Brilliant is incredibly user-friendly for a plug-and-play system, but it cannot match the deep, hardware-level programming and limitless scalability of an enterprise-grade luxury platform.

Why Bespoke Luxury Systems Outperform DIY Solutions

For a luxury residence in neighborhoods like Beverly Hills, Pacific Palisades, or Palos Verdes Estates, a DIY or semi-DIY system like Brilliant can sometimes fall short of expectations. Here is why bespoke luxury systems remain the gold standard:

  • Uncompromising Reliability: High-end systems are hardwired, meaning they do not suffer from the latency, interference, or dropouts common to consumer Wi-Fi networks.
  • Invisible Intelligence: At PROJECT: automate, our philosophy is to hide the technology. Instead of placing plastic touchscreens in every single room, we use elegant, custom-engraved solid metal keypads that blend seamlessly into your interior design, keeping the actual hardware hidden away in a central equipment rack.
  • Dedicated Support: When a DIY system has an issue, you are left troubleshooting on online forums or waiting for email support. With a professionally installed system, you have access to proactive monitoring and rapid, on-site support to ensure your home runs flawlessly 24/7.

Pros, Cons, Pricing, and Brilliant Max

If you decide that Brilliant is the right fit for your project, it is important to weigh the pros, cons, and ongoing costs:

Pros:

  • Extremely easy for guests and children to use without training.
  • Eliminates countertop voice assistant clutter by putting Alexa in the wall.
  • Excellent native integrations with Sonos, Ring, and Nest.
  • Beautiful digital photo frame feature.

Cons:

  • Wired panels require neutral and ground wires, which can limit installation in older historic homes.
  • Wi-Fi dependent; if your home router crashes, many smart integrations stop working.
  • No native support for 240V electrical systems (limited to US and Canada).

Pricing & Subscription:

  • 1-Switch Panel: $599
  • 2-Switch Panel: $649
  • 3-Switch Panel: $669
  • 4-Switch Panel: $749
  • Brilliant Max Subscription: To unlock advanced, self-learning automation modes that adapt to your daily routines without manual programming, Brilliant offers a subscription service called Brilliant Max for $9.99/month or $99/year (which includes a 30-day free trial).

Frequently Asked Questions about Brilliant Smart Home Control

Does Brilliant require a neutral wire for installation?

Yes, the standard wired Brilliant Control panels require a neutral wire, a ground wire, a line wire, and a load wire inside the electrical box. If your home was built before the mid-1980s, you may not have neutral wires. In that case, you can opt for the Brilliant Plug-In Control Panel, which mounts to any wall and plugs into a standard electrical outlet without requiring any changes to your in-wall wiring.

Can I use Brilliant without a Wi-Fi connection?

Brilliant requires a 2.4 GHz (or 5 GHz on Gen 2 models) Wi-Fi connection for its initial setup and to communicate with partner smart home devices like Sonos, Ring, and Nest. If your Wi-Fi or internet goes down, you will still be able to use the physical sliders on the panel to turn your local, wired lights on and off. However, you will lose access to smart integrations, the room-to-room video intercom, and voice control via Amazon Alexa until your network connection is restored.

What is the Brilliant Max subscription?

Brilliant Max is an optional subscription service priced at $9.99/month or $99/year. It introduces intelligent, pre-configured automation modes that automatically adjust your lighting, climate, and music throughout the day based on your household’s natural habits. This eliminates the need for you to manually program complex schedules or scenes, allowing your home to intelligently run itself.

Conclusion

The brilliant home control system has rightfully earned its spot as one of the most innovative consumer smart home products on the market. By transforming the humble light switch into an elegant, centralized touchscreen, it solves the problem of smart home fragmentation for thousands of homeowners.

However, if you are building or renovating a high-end estate in Malibu, Beverly Hills, or the Hollywood Hills, your home deserves an automation system that is as elegant, reliable, and unique as your architecture.

At PROJECT: automate, we specialize in designing and installing bespoke luxury smart-home systems that deliver “invisible intelligence”—discreet, ultra-reliable technology that enhances your lifestyle without cluttering your walls. Whether you want to explore state-of-the-art Light Control solutions, optimize your estate’s Energy Management, or design a fully integrated home theater, we are here to bring your vision to life.

Ready to elevate your living space? Transform your home with professional light control and experience the true power of luxury home automation. Contact us today to schedule your private consultation.

This is probably the most obvious device you’ll need for a stellar surround sound system. To experience truly immersive entertainment, you’ll need at least five high-end speakers: one on the left, one on the right, one in the center, and two in the back. This will help you enjoy the sound from every direction around you, making it more realistic and fully immersing you in the action on your screen.

A World-Class Receiver 

You should never underestimate the power of an exemplary receiver! But what is this device, and why does your surround sound system need it?
Great question! Receivers (also known as “amps” by some people) are devices that take in signals from an audio source, such as a Blu-ray player, then process that sound to clear it up, amplify it and then send it to your speakers to deliver crisp, lifelike audio. Adding this to your surround sound installation is one of the best ways to ensure you enjoy every detail of your audio content with unmatched quality.

A Powerful Subwoofer 

Subwoofers are devices that produce low frequencies that standard surround sound setups cannot deliver on their own. These frequencies rank from 20-200 Hz, and they are perfect for boosting your experience when listening to music that relies heavily on kick drums or bass guitars. In addition, subwoofers are perfect for creating a realistic experience if you are an avid action movie fan, as you’ll be able to hear sound effects, such as explosions, much clearer.
